findings.finding: The round-6 narrowing reached the ADR and the backlog row but not the notes. backlog-notes.md:250 prescribes '`CommitDelta` carries the triple PER `SegmentCommit`', and 'the triple' is defined throughout this commit as `(podId, incarnationId, flushSeq)` (ADR :62, :84; M4.10d row). ADR-0036:99 says the exact opposite in capitals -- '⚠️ NOT `podId`' -- and the M4.10c row in backlog.md agrees ('not `podId`, already in the segment key'). The ADR itself repeats the stale word at :111, 'Give those fixtures DIFFERENT triples per segment', describing a field set its own decision two lines earlier forbids.
findings.failure_scenario: AGENTS.md directs a session to read the notes for the one task it picks. A session picking M4.10c reads backlog-notes.md:250, adds `podId` to `SegmentCommit` alongside `incarnationId` and `flushSeq`, and lands it in the one commit that must change both delta encodings, both readers, the fakes and the goldens (non-negotiable 8). The result contradicts an accepted ADR in bytes that outlive the process, and puts two independent pod attributions on one record -- `podId` beside a `segmentKey` that already embeds `podShortId` -- with nothing forcing them to agree, which is the hazard ADR-0036:101 rejects the field for. Reversing it costs a second wire-format commit. This is the fix-one-copy-miss-the-duplicate shape baselines/review.txt already records for M4.10a ('deleting the section missed its duplicate') and for M4.8's split.
findings.remedy: Replace 'the triple' at backlog-notes.md:250 with `(incarnationId, flushSeq)` and say why podId is excluded; fix 'triples' at ADR :111.

findings.finding: The sole ground for dropping `podId` from the delta is stated as a property of the record, and it is a property of one caller. ADR :99 'SegmentCommit.segmentKey is a rendered SegmentKey, which already carries podShortId' and :114 'podShortId does travel inside every segmentKey' are both false of the type and of this tree. `SegmentCommit.segmentKey` is a `String` checked only for non-emptiness (SegmentCommit.java:29-31); `CommitRequest.segmentKey` only for non-blank (CommitRequest.java:60-62); nothing anywhere requires it to have been rendered by `SegmentKey`. `SegmentKey` exposes no podShortId accessor at all -- `headerLenOf` (SegmentKey.java:212) is its only parser and it throws IllegalArgumentException('not a segment key: ...') on every segment key in the sequencer and format suites ('seg/a', 'seg/b', 'bins/pod1/0.bseg', 'seg-clash') and on the golden the ADR itself cites: `golden/chain-delta-batched-v1.bin` holds `bins/a.seg` and `bins/b.seg`, which carry no pod attribution whatsoever. The identity holds only because DefaultIngest passes one constructor argument to both the publisher and the request (DefaultIngest.java:143-146, :349). The ADR does not say so, and does not name the extraction the decision now requires.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.10c/d must do two things the ADR mandates and neither can be done from the delta as narrowed. (a) 'a successor can rebuild the window from the uncheckpointed tail' (:97): the window is per pod (the checkpoint slot is keyed by podId, and CheckpointWriter.capture:129 merges on `request.podId()`), but the tail now carries no podId. On a first takeover with no predecessor checkpoint -- the case CheckpointWriter's own class javadoc names, 'its first checkpoint carries no pods at all' -- the tail is the only source and there is no podId anywhere in it, so the successor cannot write those entries into its own next checkpoint under any key. The window is therefore lost at the first post-takeover checkpoint, which is exactly 'a takeover loses every commit made since the predecessor's last checkpoint' (:115), the harm this bullet claims to fix, deferred by one checkpoint instead of removed. (b) 'answer only if it carries that exact (podId, incarnationId, flushSeq)' (:73): the pointed delta carries no podId to compare. The natural repair is to parse podShortId out of segmentKey, which needs a parser that does not exist over a field nothing constrains; every fixture and the golden fail that parse, so the parse failure gets caught and the pod skipped -- yielding an empty recovered window, a state ADR-0036 itself declares ACCEPTED rather than refused (:135-138). Dedup then silently no-ops across the very takeover it exists for while every test stays green: the identical 'total no-op in production while every sequencer-seam test passes' failure the ADR names for the minting site at :34. And the hazard the narrowing was meant to remove is relocated rather than removed -- the checkpoint slot's identity comes from `CommitRequest.podId` and the chain's from a substring of a caller-supplied string, two independent attributions with nothing forcing them to agree.
findings.remedy: One clause in the CommitDelta bullet: state that the attribution is recoverable only from a key rendered by `SegmentKey`, name the mechanism (either an extraction M4.10c must add plus a constraint on `CommitRequest.segmentKey`, or that the recovered window is keyed on `incarnationId` alone and podId serves only the checkpoint slot), and record that no fixture or golden in the tree renders a real segment key today, so M4.10c pays for that either way.

findings.finding: '**No commit-path request scales with pods.** Detection is an in-memory comparison' discharges the row's third property using only half the mechanism. The ADR's own answering rule (:73-79, :130) is one GET of the pointed delta per replayed request, and the pointer is per pod, so the answering half does sit on the commit path and does scale with the pods that replay.
findings.failure_scenario: A takeover is when replays happen. N in-flight pods retry into one `commitAll` window -- the batching primitive M4.7 exists for -- and each detected replay costs a GET of that pod's pointed delta, so one commit window issues N GETs. If those pods' last-applied commits were batched into one delta, which is the normal case under M4.7, they are N GETs of the SAME key with nothing in the decision saying to coalesce them (rule R4's shape). Non-negotiable 6 permits scaling with nodes, so this is not a violation of it; but the row's stated property is stricter ('no COMMIT-PATH request that scales with the number of pods -- the rate M4.7 was built to remove'), and a future session will cite this unqualified sentence as having settled it.
findings.remedy: Qualify the sentence: detection is free, answering costs one GET per replayed request and is coalescable per delta within a batch.

findings.finding: `### M4.10b` is left as an open brief for work this commit lands. It still says 'Whether any of that suffices is this ADR's finding, not this row's', '⚠️ ADR-0031 IS ADJACENT, NOT ANSWER ... Say whether its argument extends', and lists 'the properties the decision must satisfy' -- all in the imperative, none recording what was decided, and with no pointer to ADR-0036. The archive row that replaced it in backlog-done.md carries no [notes] link, so the section is orphaned as well as stale.
findings.failure_scenario: A session picking M4.10c or M4.10d greps M4.10 in backlog-notes and reads a brief instructing it to answer questions ADR-0036 has already answered -- including 'say whether ADR-0031's argument extends', which the ADR answers at :92 and :157. It either re-derives a settled decision or, worse, answers it differently. baselines/review.txt records this exact shape being found and fixed by deletion at M4.10a round 3, 'a backlog-notes section written in pre-fix present tense'.
findings.remedy: Reduce the section to what the archive row's essay needs -- the measurement that killed the segment key and the properties as DISCHARGED -- or point it at ADR-0036 in one line.
